items.t: Announced that the process of implementing the voter ID law begins on the day of the Shelby County v. Holder decision, and said he intended to finalize draft regulations to implement the law on August 1 (2013).
items.q: he announced that the process for implementing the voter ID law “begins today.” Just a few days later, I received Hosemann’s letter informing me that he intends to finalize his draft regulations to implement the law on August 1.

items.t: Fought to enact a constitutional Voter ID law as Secretary of State.
items.q: As Secretary of State, Lt. Governor Hosemann revised Mississippi’s business laws, automated legal filings, and fought to enact a constitutional Voter ID law.

items.t: Advocates for increasing state government transparency.
items.q: He advocates for increasing state government transparency, growing small businesses, shoring up Mississippi’s roads and bridges, providing better access to healthcare, and ensuring every child receives a high-quality education.

record.t: Was re-elected to a second term as Lieutenant Governor with more than 60 percent of the vote.
record.q: Re-elected to a second term in November 2023 with more than 60 percent of the vote, the Honorable Delbert Hosemann is serving as Mississippi’s 33rd Lieutenant Governor.

record.t: Said the Presidential Advisory Commission on Election Integrity should "go jump in the Gulf of Mexico" in response to its request for sensitive state data.
record.q: Several secretaries of state, Republican and Democrat, bucked a request for sensitive data by the commission or said they would only provide limited data. Mississippi Secretary of State Delbert Hosemann, a Republican, suggested the commission “go jump in the Gulf of Mexico.”

record.t: Served as Secretary of State, including requiring 16th Section land to be leased for fair value.
record.q: Lt. Governor Hosemann’s tenure as Secretary of State was marked by several major accomplishments including requiring 16th Section land, a revenue source for public schools, to be leased for fair value.

record.t: Led the Legislature as it implemented a teacher pay raise and a tax cut described as the largest in state history.
record.q: Under Lt. Governor Hosemann’s leadership, the Mississippi Legislature implemented the largest teacher pay raise and largest tax cut in state history

record.t: Led the Legislature as it paid off $1.2 billion in state debt and developed a new student-centered school funding formula.
record.q: developed a new student-centered funding formula for schools, retooled economic development incentives to be competitive and performance-based, and paid off $1.2 billion in state debt.
